title: The US-Canada Border Is 5,500 Miles of Pure Nonsense
beats: Longest, straightest, most boring border, yet look closer and it is bizarre
The no-touching-zone: a 20-foot cleared strip along the whole border, with exceptions
You would assume deforested means straight; it is not, the real line is 900 zig-zag segments
You are a 1800s surveyor with a compass and string told to mark the 49th parallel
Surveyors did their best; 900 monuments, strip connects the dots; about 8,000 markers total
Disputed Atlantic islands: Canada built a lighthouse, the US pretends it is not there
Zoom on the odd upward tick and lake detour into Canada
1783 negotiators used a map whose key area was hidden under an inset, so they bordered blind
They guessed a line to the Mississippi, which stops short, leaving border vague 35 years
Second treaty set the 49th, but lake was higher so border jumps up then drops, cutting off a bit of Canada
Straight lines over hundreds of miles cause problems: Vancouver Island caught, Point Roberts missed
Point Roberts kids cross the border four times a day to reach school in their own state
East coast mirror case; spot such enclaves in satellite photos via the strip

theory: Grey states the expected thing, then breaks it (straight-looking border is not straight), then gives a causal story that explains every later oddity. One cause (drawing straight lines on unknown land) is reused across examples, so each new case is predicted, not memorized.
velocity: Orchestrator: open with expectation then break it, scene shows the straight map then zoom to jagged reality
Scene builder: zoom-in on a single anomaly after the whole-map view
